territorial_scope.description: Applies to City of Boise departments, agencies and entities, and to third-party contractors and vendors working with the City on AI projects.

evidence.quote: This regulation applies to all city departments, agencies, and entities involved in the development, procurement, deployment, or use of AI technologies.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Sets internal rules for City of Boise departments, agencies and entities that develop, procure, deploy or use AI, including generative AI. Requires IT approval before acquiring AI products, human fact-checking of AI output, disclosure of AI use in significant public communications, and no sensitive data in prompts. Effective 12-1-23.
summary.long: The regulation governs the City of Boise's use of artificial intelligence. It covers city departments, agencies and entities that develop, procure, deploy or use AI, and third-party contractors or vendors working with the City on AI projects. It applies to all forms of AI, with particular attention to generative AI, and is described as an interim resource for City employees. Employees must obtain IT Department approval before accessing or acquiring an AI product, and IT maintains a list of approved AI products. New commercial software with an AI capability requires answers to listed questions on training data, data access and whether the AI component can be disabled. Staff must fact-check and review AI-generated content, especially for public communication or decisions, and must reference AI use in significant public communications. Sensitive or private information, including personal data about employees and community members, must not be placed in prompts. The Information Technology department oversees AI initiatives with sponsoring departments, runs an ongoing evaluation and monitoring process, and conducts periodic audits. The regulation is to be reviewed annually. The text sets out no penalties or enforcement mechanisms.

relations.note: Cross-reference to a city Employee Handbook regulation on personnel files, not in the registry. Section 4.D refers to it for protecting employee personal information in prompts; section 8 says it defines requirements for protecting employee privacy.

evidence.quote: Employee Handbook – 4.45a Personnel Files Regulation. Defines requirements for protecting employee privacy.

notes: Header gives Effective 12-1-23 and leaves Revised blank. Section 4.C says to reference AI use as 'see Paragraph 1 above', but the text's section 1 is Regulation Purpose and no paragraph refers to AI use. The Scope section extends the regulation to third-party contractors and vendors, but no operative provision separately addresses them. The regulation says part of its content was generated by ChatGPT v3.5. No legal basis, amendment, repeal or implementation relation is stated in the text.

thresholds.note: The document contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its numbers are the regulation number (4.30q), the effective date (12-1-23), the ChatGPT v3.5 reference, the annual review period in Section 5.A (a procedural time limit, not a threshold) and the cross-referenced handbook regulation 4.45a.
